title: Belonging Interrupted: Toward an Understanding of How Virtual Learning Impedes Women Students’ Belonging in Engineering
body_coverage: Full Introduction, Review of Literature, Methods, three Findings sections, Discussion including practice/research limitations, Conclusion and Notes; Tables 1–3. Journey-map figures not visually checked; textual descriptions alone used. Cited references not individually retraced.
design: Seven March-2022 focus groups at one Mid-Atlantic U.S. research institution with 21 women and one non-binary student, all assigned female at birth; eight then in third year (remote during second year), fourteen then in fourth year (remote during third year). Transcripts, journey maps and challenge/resolution cards analyzed. Pandemic focus emerged from accounts, not a planned pandemic questioning route.
parse_check: Native section order and three linked tables read. Table 3 transcript salience 7/8 versus 8/14 refers to coded representation of COVID, not a risk difference in clinical distress or belonging scores. Participant nicknames map consistently across tables and text; figure-only trajectories not used.

moves.problem: A single adverse effect of remote learning cannot explain why some accounts describe an opportunity.
locations: Findings:Remote Experiences in Second College Year
Findings:Remote Experiences in Third College Year
moves.author_move: Contrasts entering the major remotely without established peers with moving established relationships online. Anna finds virtual office hours awkward; Kalea, with existing professor relationships, finds them less intimidating. The same communication format carries different meanings depending on relational history.
moves.project_inference: Use the same activity across cases to sharpen a conditional explanation, rather than infer a blanket technology effect. The contrast identifies relational history as an explanation worth checking, not a causally identified moderator.
moves.condition: Cohorts differ in stage, courses and experiences; do not treat focus-group differences as an experimental timing effect or a universal trajectory.

moves.problem: A favorable case is absorbed into the main theme, hiding what support cannot do.
locations: Findings:COVID-19 Exacerbated External Challenges Irrespective of Class Year
moves.author_move: Revisits Caroline, whose academic focus later improved after leaving an unstable home, and Mila, whose established friendships could be sources of racialized stress. These accounts limit a simple proposition that existing community protects students.
moves.project_inference: Let a case revise a proposed relationship: connections may provide resources but their quality and material conditions matter. Preserve external explanations rather than rename every difficulty belonging uncertainty.
moves.condition: Do not impose chronology beyond what the named account supplies; self-reported outcomes were not independently audited.

do_not_adopt: The findings' conditional variation is more defensible than the title's blanket language that virtual learning impedes belonging.
Counterfactual statements that relationships would have protected students or will prevent engineering-career attrition exceed this design.
Less gender-performance pressure online is a proposed alternative interpretation in Discussion, not a measured mechanism in these focus groups.
COVID salience in artefacts cannot establish effect magnitude or population incidence.
Do not describe all participants as women without retaining the non-binary participant and recruitment based on administrative sex data.
